name: Wrenchy: Car Service Log
subtitle: Oil Change & Tire Reminders
promotionalText: Every oil change, tire swap and repair your car has had, on your phone. No account, no server, nothing to sync and nothing to lose. CSV export is free for everyone.
description:
Your service records, kept for good. On your phone, not on somebody else's server.

Most car maintenance apps want an account, a sync, and a bit of luck. One broken login and years of service history are gone. Wrenchy works the other way: no account, no server, nothing to sync. Every oil change, tire rotation and repair you log stays on the phone.

WHAT IT DOES
- Log oil changes, tire rotations, brakes, filters, coolant, spark plugs, a safety inspection, or anything else you type in, for as many vehicles as you keep
- Get a reminder the day the next one is due, by date or by kilometres, whichever comes first
- See the full maintenance history for each vehicle at a glance
- Export the whole log to CSV whenever you want. Export is free for everyone and never sits behind the subscription

NO ANNUAL TEST MEANS NO DEADLINE
Most countries run a yearly roadworthiness test that drags the rest of the maintenance along with it. Canada does not, for passenger cars in most provinces. Nothing arrives to tell you the car is overdue. What actually falls due is what the manufacturer set: oil at its interval, tire rotation, brake fluid, coolant, the timing belt. The only thing tracking that is you. Wrenchy holds each interval by date and by kilometres and tells you on the day.

Safety Inspection and Plate Renewal are in the list as well. The check you book before a private sale or when a car comes in from another province, and the renewal that comes around every year or two.

THE SEASONAL PART
The tire changeover is the one job a Canadian owner never forgets and never writes down. Log the swap each fall and each spring and you end up with the dates, the shop, and the kilometres each set has actually run. Winter tires that have quietly done six seasons stop being a guess.

WHY IT'S DIFFERENT
No account. No login. No server. No sync to break. Your maintenance history cannot disappear, because there is nothing for it to disappear from. It sits on the phone, the way a paper logbook sat in the glovebox.

BUILT FOR REAL OWNERS
- Unlimited service records across multiple vehicles
- Custom intervals for oil, rotations, brakes, air and cabin filters, coolant, and anything else you run on a schedule
- Due by odometer or due by date, whichever lands first, in kilometres
- Dark, glare-friendly screens meant to be read in a driveway in February or across a service counter

WHO IT'S FOR
Daily drivers, DIY mechanics, people who flip cars, and anyone who will eventually sell privately. A buyer asks how the car was looked after, and a complete log answers that better than a shoebox of receipts. Every oil change, every repair note, every inspection date, in one searchable place.

Free for one vehicle. Wrenchy Pro adds unlimited vehicles and custom service intervals. Export stays free, for everyone.

notes.reasoning: The harvest breaks into six Canadian intents and the indexed bag covers all six with no word spent twice. NAME takes the cleanest high-intent cluster, car maintenance, plus log, which also reaches maintenance logs, car maintenance book, car maintenance tracker and car maintenance reminders. SUBTITLE takes the two things the name cannot reach and that Canadians actually type: oil change reminder, harvested verbatim, and tire, which is the only automotive word behind the winter tire seed. That seed is worth noting on its own: every suggestion it returned was a golf club, a snow globe or a dress-up game, so winter tire is a real Canadian intent with no app competing for it, and tire sits in the subtitle rather than the keyword field because of that. KEYWORDS carry only words used nowhere else and recombine with the name and subtitle: vehicle, service, history, tracker, mileage, odometer, repair, records, brakes, rotation, winter, care, book. Rejected as other apps' names, not queries: aracpro, ato vehicle logbook, autocards, autosist, beepster, cafu, car assistant, car cave, car chronicle, car care inc., car care fuel & service log, carfax car care, carfax canada car care, chapincity car service, costa oil, driveledger, maintenance care, maintenance iq, maintenance iq by yardi, mileage iq, mileage plus, mileage tracker by driversnote, mileage tracker by mileiq, milecare vehicle service log, repo vehicle photos, vehicle info, vehicle leasing system, vehicle loancalc, vehicle log vault, vehicle logger, vehicle masters, vehicle speed, 20-20 car service, car service 2.0, car service book - auto log, car service tracker - autozis, and every game (car maintenance game, car repair game, car repair center 3d, car repair shop simulator, car repair garage games, car service mechanic simulator, car service station parking, vehicle games, winter tiles matching, winter world games 2026, winter sports mania, winter survival, eternal winter, winter fireplace, winter snow globe, winter time with warm dressup, calgary winter club, the dunes golf & winter club, car camera, car camping, car cast). Car maintenance log - glovebox is our own listing. Deliberately left out: logbook, because in Canada mileage logbook and mileage tracker canada are overwhelmingly CRA business-trip intent, which this app does not serve, and chasing it buys the wrong installs; mileage stays as a single keyword because odometer-based due dates are genuinely what it does. Also left out: safety, inspection, plate, registration. They are the Canada-specific services the app names, but none of them appear anywhere in the harvest, so they earn description space rather than indexed characters. On the missing legal test: Canada has no general periodic inspection, so the reminder pitch has no legal deadline to lean on and none is invented. The description says so outright in NO ANNUAL TEST MEANS NO DEADLINE and turns the absence into the argument, since nothing external will tell an owner the car is overdue, which makes manufacturer intervals, the fall and spring tire changeover, and a complete record for private resale the three things the reminders exist for. Safety Inspection and Plate Renewal are named exactly as the in-app en-CA overlay names them, framed as a pre-sale or out-of-province check and a recurring renewal rather than as a test that falls due by law. Distances are kilometres throughout, spelling is US except kilometres, and no claim is made beyond the fact list. Not verifiable from the harvest: relative search volume between clusters, since autocomplete returns suggestions rather than counts, so the name choice ranks car maintenance above vehicle log on cluster cleanliness rather than measured demand.

whatsNew:
Fixed a bug that could show the same service as due and overdue at the same time.

The first-run screens are clearer too, and the reminder preview now matches your device's light or dark appearance.
